public_rationale: Contemporary reporting supports the view that human staffing made expansion costly and that the original service remained restricted. The 10,000 figure also has contemporary support. However, another report gives roughly 2,000 testers, and the records do not explain the difference. Costs and their accounting basis are undisclosed. These gaps prevent a firm verdict on the combined claim.
limitations: The cost claim has an unknown accounting basis and cannot receive a supported or contradicted financial score under the specified rules.
Different access-count definitions could explain the conflicting reports.
The available causal explanation comes from reporting rather than disclosed internal decision records.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Facebook M was expensive to run, so it reached only about 10,000 users and was never scaled to the general public.

statement.excerpt: Part of the problem was that M was expensive for Facebook to run; so they only rolled it to about 10,000 users, and never scaled it to the general public.

from_speaker: never scaled it to the general public
our_interpretation: Operating expense must have contributed materially to limiting the original concierge service; it need not have been the sole cause.
About 10,000 refers to people given access, rather than monthly active users or users of M Suggestions.
Expensive means sufficiently costly to constrain expansion. No spending amount or accounting basis is supplied.
The target period covers the stated launch year through the stated cancellation month.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes roughly 10,000 recipients of access, no general release of the original service, and operating expense as a material reason for limiting expansion.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records establish a materially different access count, a general release of the original service, or that expense did not materially constrain expansion.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Facebook records reconciling access counts, together with operating-cost evidence and a documented explanation of how expense affected the rollout decision.
